files.description: Clinic appointments in New York (160 rows, February to November 2025, so the clock changes in March and November fall inside the data): appt_id (whole number), local_start (New York wall-clock start, text YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, no UTC offset), start_with_offset (the same moment as ISO text with its UTC offset, e.g. "2025-06-13T08:45:00-04:00"), clinic (Harbor, Midtown or Riverside; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), duration_min (whole minutes; about 3% empty).

task_text: For each appointment a check-up is booked 14 calendar days later at the same New York wall-clock time (local_start is New York local time). Count how many check-ups start in each hour of the New York day. `result` should be a Series indexed by hour (0-23) with the number of check-ups, only for hours that occur.
intended_computation: The check-up keeps the local clock time, so its local hour equals the appointment's hour; count the 160 check-ups per local hour.

predicted_direction.reason: on 2.x the day offset adds 14 x 24 hours, so check-ups across the clock change land one hour off; 3.x keeps the local hour

notes: Drafted 2026-11-11 in package TASKS_M1; task text, card, naive solution, reference and predicted direction were prepared there.
